text:
Maya K: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting 503s on hosted streaming/embed endpoints since ~11:09 PST. High QPS, several sessions dropped mid-stream.
Support-bot: alert: hosted.inference.error_rate > 5% (11:10) — affected clusters: cluster-east-2
Maya K: Customer sample: "upstream inference worker failed, returning 503". They sent a stack: `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` and `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory`.
Alex M: Noted. Any recent deploys?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout inference-runtime:v2.13 to cluster-east-2 started at 11:08:53 by jenkins/infer-release
Josh L: I'm looking at runner logs for pod infer-runner-7f8d. grabbing tail now.
Josh L: `kubectl -n hosted logs infer-runner-7f8d -c infer --tail=120` shows:
```
2024-05-04T11:09:21Z ERROR runtime: worker(0) received SIGSEGV
2024-05-04T11:09:21Z INFO  crash_handler: saving /var/crash/core.1234
2024-05-04T11:09:22Z ERROR infer: RuntimeError: CUDA illegal memory access
2024-05-04T11:09:22Z INFO  watcher: process 1234 exited with code 139, restarting
```
Josh L: dmesg on node shows: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus` and `Out of memory: Killed process 1234 (python) total-vm=...`
Priya S: nvtop / nvidia-smi at crash time?
Josh L: pulled `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv` from node: `memory.used [MiB] = 31875 MiB, memory.total [MiB] = 32768 MiB` (one container using ~31.1GB).
Emily R: That suggests a memory spike during a batched streaming request — KV cache growth + long contexts. Any correlation with batch size change?
Maya K: Customer said they sent 6 concurrent streaming requests with ~60k token contexts.
Alex M: If deploy v2.13 changed attention cache eviction or prefetch heuristics, could cause mem growth under long contexts.
Priya S: Repro steps requested from CS: how to recreate. Maya, can you ask for a minimal repro (prompt shape + concurrency)?
Maya K: FYI asked customer for a repro snippet. They sent back a short harness: 6 parallel requests, prompt ~120k chars, model: gpt-open-16k (hotloaded).
Josh L: Running local repro now on staging with similar workload. I can reproduce memory climb and eventual segfault within ~90s.
Josh L: Quick log snippet from staging: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` then `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`.
Emily R: Immediate mitigation options?
Alex M: 1) Add short-term routing rule: route this customer to a smaller-context model (8k) or to cpu-quantized fallback to avoid OOM. 2) Throttle max concurrent streams per token-length. 3) Roll back v2.13 to v2.12 if we confirm regression.
Priya S: Support recommends throttling + routing change to reduce customer impact while we triage. Maya, can you apply a per-customer throttle and enable fallback?
Maya K: Doing that now — setting max_concurrent_streams=2 and fallback_model=gpt-open-8k for customer acme-prod.
Maya K: Done. Customer reports 503s stopped within ~2m after change. :white_check_mark:
Josh L: On the runtime side, initial root cause looks like evictions in KV cache not freeing memory fast enough during batched preprefetch; with long contexts the accumulated allocations exceed GPU mem and NV driver gives Xid31. I'm collecting heap snapshots and core dumps.
Josh L: gdb backtrace from core:
```
#0  0x00007f9a12c3b1a0 in cuMemAlloc_v2 () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1
#1  0x00007f9a1a2e5b3f in some_cuda_wrapper
#2  0x000055a4b8f3c1a2 in model::allocate_kv_cache()
#3  0x000055a4b8f3f5cc in runtime::prefetch_worker()
```
Josh L: Filing runtime bug with core + nvml traces. Will attach heap snapshot and exact command line.
Alex M: Thanks. Can we add guardrails to the runtime to fail the request politely when predicted mem > device_free - margin (instead of attempting alloc)?
Emily R: That's a good hardening item. Add to backlog: predictive-allocation-check + early-fail with friendly 429/413 instead of crash.
Priya S: I'll coordinate release prioritization. Josh, what's ETA for a hotfix?
Josh L: I can push a defensive check (cap per-request KV allocations) and a small prefetch throttle in ~4 hours, then smoke test in staging. If green, rollout to cluster-east-2 tonight.
Maya K: I'll keep customer notified and keep fallback in place.
Alex M: Also check autoscaler behavior — currently the pod restarts are noisy and routed traffic causes cascade. Maybe add temporary increase to pod pool to avoid restarts while fix rolls out.
Josh L: Increasing replica count + bumping restart-backoff to 60s for the group now.
Maya K: Noted. CS requested a short incident blurb for the customer explaining cause and mitigation. Drafting and will share.
Priya S: Owner checklist: Josh = runtime fix + PR, Alex = autoscaler/routing change, Maya = CS comms + customer throttle, Emily = backlog item for predictive-alloc.
Maya K: I'll open the customer ticket with the mitigation summary and link the bug: BUG-4821.
Josh L: Bug created: BUG-4821 — "prefetch + long-context -> KV cache accumulation -> cuda OOM/Xid31 -> segfault". Attachments: core + nvml logs + repro harness.
Alex M: Good work shipping short-term mitigation. Postmortem + rollout plan please once runtime fix is deployed.
Maya K: Will do. Closing thread after follow-up items are tracked. :spiral_note_pad:
